key_decisions.decision: Preserves the repeated attending verb as a reversal from failed care to accountability.
Keeps divine responsibility for dispersal and the fruitful-and-multiply language.
Retains future care, freedom from fear, and the assurance that none are missing.
Retains the growth image and the king's wisdom and justice without identifying a later individual in the translation.
Preserves both kingdoms and the royal name while leaving its theological implications to interpretation.
Preserves the source's first-person shift within the oath and the return to their own ground.
Follows the read form 'his word' and preserves the challenge about access to the divine council.
Gives the elliptical question readable English while retaining the repeated heart and lying-prophecy language.
Preserves the claim to an oracle without inserting an additional divine name into the quoted formula.
Follows the pinned word division 'What burden?' and keeps burden as the oracle word needed for the following wordplay.
Keeps the prohibition's three groups and household consequence.
Preserves the two acceptable questions and the brother wording rather than broadening every relationship.
Retains the burden reversal and the full identification of the living God.
Keeps the repeated questions now directed to a prophet.
Preserves all repetitions of the prohibited formula and leaves the sentence open for its consequence.
Follows the pointed forgetting verb while flagging the difficult accompanying form and alternative burden wordplay in a note.
